title: Origins and Road to War
sub: How the War of Dagestan began

slides.title: From First Chechen War to War of Dagestan
slides.cap: Historical connection: Chechen conflict spreads into Dagestan
slides.body: The unresolved First Chechen War left armed Islamist factions operating from Chechnya. Their invasion of neighboring Dagestan attempted to spread rebellion across the North Caucasus.

stats.lbl: The unresolved First Chechen War left armed Islamist factions operating from Chechnya. Their invasion of neighboring Dagestan attempted to spread rebellion across the North Caucasus.

slides.title: Before the War of Dagestan
slides.body:
Islamist fighters based in Chechnya entered Dagestan hoping to trigger an uprising and establish a broader Islamic state.

The Conflict Takes Shape: The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus. The opening phase established the political goals, alliances, and military problems that shaped every later campaign.

stats.val: The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus.

slides.title: Battle of Karamakhi
slides.body:
Battle of Karamakhi marked an important episode in the War of Dagestan. It showed how the conflict's political goals were being translated into military action and placed new pressure on both the battlefield and surrounding communities.

Why This Moment Matters: Battle of Karamakhi was more than an isolated engagement. It helped define the conflict's direction and exposed the strengths and weaknesses of the opposing sides. The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus.

Consequences: The effects of Battle of Karamakhi extended beyond its immediate result. Mountain villages became battlefields, civilians fled, and subsequent violence contributed to a much wider renewed war in Chechnya. Its place in the wider campaign also influenced later military choices and political calculations.

slides.title: Tukhchar massacre
slides.body:
The Tukhchar massacre was an incident during the War in Dagestan which was filmed and distributed on tape, in which Russian prisoners of war were executed. Throughout the battle, Russian soldiers reported finding taped executions of Russian officers and men. Some videos were later sold as snuff films and ended up being posted online. One tape created in September 1999 showed six Russian servicemen, five as young as 19, who were conscripts, being executed by Chechen and Dagestani militants. The method was piercing the trachea, also known as beheading.

Why This Moment Matters: Tukhchar massacre was more than an isolated engagement. It reflected the changing balance of power and pushed the conflict closer to its eventual outcome. The incursion challenged Russian federal authority and threatened to spread insurgency across the North Caucasus.

title: International and Human Dimensions
sub: The wider impact of the War of Dagestan

slides.title: International Dimension
slides.body:
Foreign fighters joined the militants, but the campaign remained primarily a Russian and Dagestani response.

The Human Cost: Mountain villages became battlefields, civilians fled, and subsequent violence contributed to a much wider renewed war in Chechnya.

title: Outcome and Legacy
sub: How the War of Dagestan ended and what followed

slides.title: The End of the War of Dagestan
slides.body: Russian forces and local Dagestani militias expelled the attackers. The crisis became the immediate prelude to the Second Chechen War.
